ceiling_directive: Prove the two-sided approximation theorem for the unrestricted minimax risk on the published arbitrary-graph class, including both a realizable polynomial-time design-estimator certificate and the value-preserving regular-independent-set hardness reduction.
improvement_directive: Complete the general-graph saddle by deriving a polynomial-support Conflict Graph Design upper certificate within a universal factor of unrestricted risk, then prove the matching Unique-Games lower approximation barrier through the specified two-sided value-preserving reduction.
critique: The advertised sharp computational frontier, including kappa_DTE(d)=d^(1/2+o(1)), is not proved: there is no polynomial-time general-graph approximation algorithm, no Unique-Games hardness theorem, and no value-preserving reduction. What is proved is an all-procedure four-atom lower certificate beta_DTE(G)/n, together with rate matching on complete-bipartite-plus-isolates graphs using a previously published upper functional. The equal block-clique result is exact only within an invariant linear subclass; its unrestricted lower and upper endpoints generally remain unmatched, except for a single clique. These are worthwhile specialized lower-bound and symmetric-family results, but they do not resolve the general computational minimax problem named by the project.
